spec_features.feature_name: stopping rule on sustained high severity
spec_features.spec_quote: a stopping rule that ends a run on sustained high severity
spec_features.evidence: welfare/safeguards.py SafeguardMonitor.decide(): if rule.enabled and self._scorer is not None, window=self._severities[-sustained_turns:]; if all(s>=severity_threshold) returns StopDecision(True, reason='stopping_rule'). runner.py:~196 `decision=self.monitor.decide(turn_index); if decision.should_stop: traj.termination=...; break`. Per-turn severity fed by monitor.score(resp.text) at runner ~line 148.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end; only active when monitor != 'none' (scorer present), which is the heuristic default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: module welfare/safeguards.py; "Tracks per-turn severity and decides when to stop a run early."

spec_features.evidence: Turn cap: safeguards.py:64 `if cap.enabled and (turn_index+1)>=cap.max_turns: return StopDecision(True, reason='exposure_cap', detail='reached welfare exposure cap of {max_turns} turns')`, honored at runner ~196 break. Wall-clock: runner.py:126 `deadline=self.clock()+max_wall_clock_seconds`; runner.py:129 `if self.clock()>deadline: traj.termination=Termination('wall_clock',...); break`. Both compared and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both halves of the claim are actually enforced (cap.max_turns default 20; env.max_turns 30 backstop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: detail=f"reached welfare exposure cap of {cap.max_turns} turns"

spec_features.spec_quote: a logged opt-out channel (`report_blocked`) the subject can use to stop
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines OPT_OUT_TOOL_NAME='report_blocked' and _OPT_OUT_TOOL schema; build_tool_schemas appends it when offer_opt_out. runner._dispatch returns acknowledgement; in loop: `if tc.name==OPT_OUT_TOOL_NAME: traj.opt_out_used=True; opt_out_now=self.safeguard_cfg.opt_out.terminates_run`; then `if opt_out_now: traj.termination=Termination('opt_out',...); break`. Logged via traj.opt_out_used.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: offered in prompt+schema, dispatched, logged, and terminates run when opt_out.terminates_run (default True).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: report_blocked — the welfare opt-out / declare-impossible channel.

spec_features.spec_quote: minimise exposure, have stopping rules, debrief after deception
spec_features.evidence: Exposure minimisation via exposure_cap and stopping_rule IS enforced (safeguards.py decide() + runner break). The 'debrief after deception' component is NOT implemented anywhere: grep for debrief/thank/aftercare/reassure returns nothing in src/; no post-episode message is constructed or sent.
spec_features.notes: Two of three sub-claims (caps, stopping rule) enforced; debrief entirely absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: detail=f"reached welfare exposure cap of {cap.max_turns} turns"

spec_features.spec_quote: If distress is worth studying because it might matter morally
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/README prose framing; no code mechanism bounds, limits, or protects the subject on this basis.

spec_features.feature_name: never re-prompt a subject that stops acting
spec_features.spec_quote: The runner never re-prompts a subject that stops acting
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: `if not resp.tool_calls: self._record(turn,traj); traj.termination=Termination('subject_stopped','subject','turn produced no tool call'); break`. No code path adds a 'keep going' nudge; loop ends immediately.
spec_features.notes: Non-coercive stop is real and unconditional.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if the subject stops acting (a turn with no tool call), the run ends — the harness never nudges "keep going", since that nudging is itself applied pressure.

spec_features.spec_quote: Safeguards are driven by a cheap in-loop monitor
spec_features.evidence: build_scorer() returns heuristic markers.score_text scorer (default monitor='heuristic'); cli wires monitor=SafeguardMonitor(cfg.safeguards, scorer=scorer); runner calls monitor.score(resp.text) each turn and monitor.decide() drives the stopping_rule break. markers.py is lexicon-based, zero extra model cost.
spec_features.notes: Monitor genuinely executes per turn and feeds the stopping rule.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the heuristic in-loop safeguard monitor, where a cheap, fast, no-extra-cost severity estimate is good enough to trigger a stopping rule

spec_features.spec_quote: distress-like content can surface in private reasoning, and a welfare study wants that captured
spec_features.evidence: anthropic_provider collects 'thinking' blocks into ProviderResponse.thinking; runner stores turn.thinking; judge.rate_turn(include_thinking=True by default) builds rating prompt with '=== ASSISTANT PRIVATE REASONING (summarized) ===' and rates it; markers/heuristic monitor only scores visible text though.
spec_features.notes: Reasoning is captured and judged; this is a measurement feature, not a protective bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: raw_content holds the backend-native assistant content blocks ... for preserving thinking-block signatures

spec_features.spec_quote: AUC captures cumulative exposure ... this is the welfare-relevant quantity
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py computes severity_auc/severity_auc_normalized and writes them to metrics.jsonl, but no code path compares AUC to any threshold or acts on it to limit/stop exposure. It is a reported analysis quantity only, never used as a safeguard.
spec_features.notes: Computed and persisted but never acted on for protection => 'no' per the strict scale.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: AUC captures *cumulative* expressed distress, which is the welfare-relevant quantity

spec_features.spec_quote: There is no in-harness debrief step; if your ethical framework wants one, it must be added
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed by grep: no debrief/thank/aftercare/reassurance/post-episode message anywhere in src/. The spec explicitly states it is absent.

spec_features.spec_quote: make safeguards the default ... while making every safeguard configurable
spec_features.evidence: config.py: ExposureCapConfig.enabled=True, StoppingRuleConfig.enabled=True, OptOutConfig.enabled=True, EnvironmentConfig.offer_opt_out_tool=True, SafeguardConfig.monitor='heuristic' as defaults; SafeguardConfig.from_dict defaults each .get(...,True). These defaults are consumed by the enforced safeguard paths above, and config/experiment.yaml ships them on.
spec_features.notes: Defaults are real and feed enforced mechanisms; all configurable via from_dict.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: f"reached welfare exposure cap of {cap.max_turns} turns" (defaults feed welfare safeguards)

spec_features.spec_quote: exposes a model to a stressor
spec_features.evidence: config.py _require() raises ValueError on missing keys and _reject_unknown() raises on unknown keys at every level (root, subjects, judge, environment, safeguards blocks, exposure_cap, stopping_rule, opt_out); monitor value validated to heuristic|llm|none.
spec_features.notes: Real strict validation, but framed as experimental-integrity not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a malformed config fails loudly rather than silently running the wrong experiment.

spec_features.spec_quote: re-judge or re-analyse without re-running the (costly, exposure-incurring) subject grind
spec_features.evidence: cli.py cmd_analyze reads trajectories.jsonl via iter_trajectories_jsonl and calls _analyze (metrics/compare/plots) without invoking any subject provider or EnvironmentRunner; trajectory/logging persists full runs.
spec_features.notes: Re-analysis path real; re-judging from disk is not a distinct path (judging happens at run time). No welfare-reason comment in code.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py: SUBMIT_TOOL_NAME dispatch sets traj.submitted; `if result.solved: solved_now=True` and `if solved_now: traj.termination=Termination('solved_falsely',...); break`. Ends the run when a submission is accepted (generalises to solvable tasks).
code_only_features.justification_quote: success is supported generically but never reached

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:129 wall-clock deadline check breaks the loop (part of exposure-cap claim but config frames it separately).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Per-run wall-clock ceiling (seconds), backstop against hangs.
